_comment: LOCAL SETTINGS PER LIBRARY, applied over whatever the registry says. Point
IIIF_LIBRARIES_FILE at this file; keep IIIF_REGISTRY_URL set as well.
Only what the registry cannot supply belongs here. It already carries every library's url,
version and name, and it is right about them — asked of all 55, every reachable instance
reported the version the registry already had. Copying those into this file would mean
maintaining a second copy of somebody else's data, which goes stale the moment it is written.
This file used to be exactly that: 38 libraries, each with the url, version and name the
registry already had, and not one local setting among them.
It is empty because there is nothing local to say yet. That is the expected state.
WHAT GOES HERE, being the three things the registry has no field for:
rps      requests per second against THIS institution's image server, overriding
IIIF_UPSTREAM_RPS. The knob to reach for after an institution asks you to ease
off. 0 disables pacing for it.
name     names by language tag, merged over the registry's PER TAG. The registry carries
exactly two — the institution's own language and English — so this is the only
way to add a third, or to correct one.
url      where this library's Kramerius is, when it is not where the registry says: a test
host, or an instance mid-migration.
version  the Kramerius version, for an instance that answers no /info. Rarely useful — the
gateway asks each instance directly and prefers that answer.
EVERY FIELD IS OPTIONAL and anything omitted comes from the registry. Naming a library here
also overrules the registry's `alive` flag, because naming it is you saying to serve it.
Keys starting with _ are notes and are ignored, including _example below.
Without IIIF_REGISTRY_URL there is nothing to inherit from, so each entry must then carry at
least a url and a version. `scripts/libraries.py --snapshot <path>` writes a complete list in
that shape, for a deployment that must not depend on the registry at runtime.
